A1.justification: Both complete, readable PDFs describe ImpMIA by the same authors. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E support reliable comparison despite the revised title and layout.

before.justification: v1 reports original membership-inference experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and CINIC-10, including baseline comparisons and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and reports additional architecture evaluations, restricted-coverage comparisons, and a pre-filtering ablation.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Appendix A retain the same gradient-based coefficient optimization, filtering, augmentation, block decomposition, aggregation, and score refinement. Newly specified scoring constants and tuning information document existing components rather than establish a revised attack procedure.

E1.justification: The main datasets and membership-inference task remain unchanged. Appendix B.2 replaces the CINIC-10-only 250K-pool experiment with a CIFAR-10 target and a pool incorporating 200K CINIC-10 images, changing the evaluated population. The scoring ablation also moves from CIFAR-100 to CIFAR-10.

E2.justification: The principal baseline set is unchanged. However, v3 adds Attack-P, Attack-R, and LiRA to the 250K-pool comparison, and those methods plus RMIA to the 10% training-coverage comparison. v1 reported only ImpMIA in these analyses.

E3.justification: v3 adds VGG16 and ResNet50 target-model evaluations and a pre-filtering on/off control. Appendix B.3 changes coverage evaluation from 5,000 to 8,000 sampled candidates, while the weight-decay study drops the 10^-6 and 10^-5 settings. These substantially extend and revise evaluation design; the main ResNet-18 recipe and evaluation metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds a direct pre-filtering ablation and comparative evidence for scalability and limited training-set coverage. It replaces the scoring and weight-decay studies with revised CIFAR-10 no-auxiliary-knowledge analyses, narrows the decay sweep, and expands runtime analysis. The former progressive assumption-removal Figure 3 is removed, although the main assumption comparisons remain.

E5.justification: Appendix A newly specifies five seeded target models for hyperparameter selection, with seeds affecting both data splits and initialization. Main-experiment averaging over five models and the standard-error reporting in v1 Tables T9–T11, retained as v3 Tables T12–T14, are unchanged. This is additional disclosure, not evidence of increased evaluation repetitions.

E6.justification: The principal benchmark and assumption-comparison values remain unchanged, but substantial supplementary results are added or replaced. New Table 2 reports ImpMIA TPR at zero FPR of 0.56% on VGG16 and 0.78% on ResNet50. The 250K-pool TPRs change from 5.49%/0.97% to 3.00%/0.54% at 0.01%/0% FPR under different data conditions, so these are replacement results, not a same-setting decline. Coverage, scoring, decay, pre-filtering, and runtime results also change.

T1.justification: The maximum-margin formulation, KKT conditions, and Appendix D weight-decay derivation are retained. Section 3.2 introduces explicit names for pairwise and minimum margins, but these restate existing expressions rather than add mathematical substance.

C1.justification: The claims of introducing implicit-bias-based membership inference and outperforming baselines without auxiliary training knowledge remain. The introduction and conclusion now explicitly claim competitiveness with leading attacks at only 10% training-set coverage, extending v1's less specific claim that partial coverage remains effective.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly discusses the possibility that pre-filtering discards genuine members and interprets its revised scoring ablation as showing that optimization drives most gains. Appendix A also revises the class-boosting rationale toward class-dependent memorization and explains why later layers are selected for CIFAR-100. These refine mechanisms and applicability without overturning the central interpretation.

D1.justification: Appendix A adds scoring constants of 0.03, 0.3, and eta=0.05, validation-data sources, and the hyperparameter-selection procedure shared across scenarios and architectures. v3 adds a project-page link and replaces H100 runtime reporting with H200 measurements in Appendix B.8. Conversely, the earlier large-pool FP16 and peak-based filtering details are omitted. These materially change reproducibility information without establishing corresponding algorithm changes.

R1.justification: v3 adds recent citations, including Pradhan et al., Shi et al., and Suri et al., with limited new discussion of hyperparameter sensitivity and distribution shifts. The central implicit-bias novelty positioning remains unchanged. The Jayaraman preprint-to-publication update concerns the same work.

P1.justification: The title is shortened, and 'No Assumptions' and 'Standard Setting' become 'No' and 'Full Auxiliary-Knowledge.' The abstract and conclusion are edited, Section 6.3 adds an appendix roadmap, and Appendix B is reorganized. Much of the prose and the overall section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from single-column to two-column presentation, with extensive changes to typography, captions, and placement. New architecture, large-pool, limited-coverage, and pre-filtering tables are added. The CIFAR-10 ROC panel moves from Figure S2 into main Figure 3, replacing the earlier assumption-removal visualization.

improvement.justification: v3 better supports practical applicability through architecture tests and direct baseline comparisons at 10% coverage and 250K candidates. Tuning disclosures and the pre-filtering control improve transparency and clarify limitations. These are useful refinements to the existing evidence, partly offset by the narrower weight-decay sweep and omission of earlier large-pool implementation details.
